Service status

This page shows whether configured feed URLs are responding, whether scheduled scoring completed, and whether the bounded European beta criteria are met. Direct liveness checks and the mirror-assisted daily run are reported separately because they measure different things. Machine-readable at /api/v1/status.json, /api/v1/run-status.json, and /api/v1/global-coverage.json.

Monitoring status and schedule

The schedule is the service commitment. The liveness record shows what the pipeline observed at each configured feed URL. Machine-readable at /api/v1/status.json.

Direct liveness calls each configured feed URL without a mirror. The daily full scoring run can use the Mobility Database mirror, so the liveness counts here and the run totals below answer different questions.

Scheduled checks

Each feed belongs to one of two direct-liveness tiers. A separate full validation is scheduled once daily for every registered feed. The latest-run section below records what that daily work completed.

CheckCadence Applies to
Priorityone direct liveness check every hourfeeds with measured realtime data, and any feed in the expiry danger or recovery window (expiring soon, or recently lapsed)
Standardone direct liveness check in each 6-hour period, on a stable per-feed schedule that spreads requests across the periodevery other tracked feed
Full Validationone full validation each dayevery registered feed

When a check fails

The scorecard keeps the last successful evidence available and makes the degraded state visible:

  • If a fetch fails, the last successful scorecard remains available. The pipeline recalculates only its calendar-based freshness and expiry fields. It never rewrites an older snapshot.
  • A feed whose calendar has been past its expiry date for more than 365 days is labeled 'stale' rather than 'lapsed', which changes how it is described but not whether it is served.
  • A configured feed URL is labeled 'unreachable' after 30 consecutive direct checks fail (roughly a week at standard cadence). This is separate from an expired calendar.
  • These observations do not guarantee an agency's GTFS host will stay online. The status page records what the pipeline observed and when.

This section is generated from the same liveness state used by the intraday refresh. It reports only observations the pipeline recorded.

Latest full scoring run

This section reports one completed scoring run. It separates all attempted records from records that remain in the current catalog and shows the age of each published score. Machine-readable at /api/v1/run-status.json.

European beta readiness

Not ready The reviewed cohort currently contains 0 GTFS Schedule feed records across 0 countries.

This is a bounded European GTFS Schedule beta gate based on feed records with reviewed reuse evidence. It is not a claim of coverage for all European public transport, and it does not assess NeTEx coverage.
